transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-20
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Chen (Redwood AE), Riley Patel (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (Solstice Head of ML), Ben Carter (Engineering Manager), Priya Singh (Data Engineer)

Summary:
Short discovery call focused on Solstice's plans to add semantic search + reranking for their clinical content portal. Main topics: where to host embeddings (Redwood hosted vs customer vector DB), throughput for embedding generation and query latency, dimensionality tradeoffs (512/768/1536), hybrid search (BM25 + vector), reranking architecture (candidate generation + LLM rerank), and security/data residency (PHI concerns). Next steps: pricing TCO, security papers, schedule deep dive and benchmark plan.

Topics:
- Current search stack and pain points
- Vector DB options and integration patterns
- Embedding dimensionality and model choices
- Throughput/backfill and online query QPS targets
- Hybrid search and reranking pipeline design
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs

Transcript:
[00:00] Jamie Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jamie from Redwood. 
[00:04] Marta Ruiz: Hi Jamie, Marta here. We had a quick agenda - we've been evaluating vector search for our clinician portal and want to understand tradeoffs.
[00:12] Ben Carter: Hi all, Ben from eng - main ask is throughput and cost. We have ~2M docs now and expect to backfill to ~11M this quarter.
[00:20] Riley Patel: Great, thanks. Quick intro from our side - I'm Riley, SE focused on embeddings and rerank. We work with both hosted embeddings and dedicated/private deployments if you need VPC or on-prem.
[00:29] Priya Singh: Quick note - some of the content may contain de-identified PHI, so data residency and KMS controls are a must.
[00:36] Jamie Chen: Totally. We'll cover SOC2, KMS/HSM options, and private control plane if needed.
[00:40] Marta Ruiz: First, how do you typically integrate with vector DBs? We currently trial Pinecone and also looked at Milvus.
[00:48] Riley Patel: Two common patterns - 1) Redwood hosts the embeddings model and you push vectors into your vector DB (Pinecone/Milvus/Weaviate), or 2) you host models in private deployment and keep everything in your VPC. With hosted we provide APIs and streaming for embeddings; you can batch ingest to your DB.
[01:01] Ben Carter: For the backfill we're worried about rate limits and time - 11M docs is non-trivial. What throughput can you sustain?
[01:10] Riley Patel: For hosted embeddings, we can do batched generation. Typical throughput numbers: with a 2x GPU pool you can generate ~1.5k-3k embeddings/sec depending on model dim and sequence length. For larger backfills we recommend parallel batched workers on your side pushing to DB in parallel; we also have guidance for exponential backoff and checkpointing. If you need faster, Dedicated capacity gives more predictable throughput and you can reserve GPUs for a backfill job.
[01:30] Marta Ruiz: What about dimensionality? We're evaluating 512 vs 1536 dims. Storage and nearest-neighbor accuracy tradeoffs are big for us.
[01:38] Riley Patel: Right - 1536 (e.g., OpenAI/Redwood higher-dim models) often gives better semantic separation for clinical nuance, but it's ~3x storage vs 512 and indexing/search cost scales. A common approach is to test both: start with 1024 or 1536 for candidate recall and then explore quantization (PQ/OPQ) in the vector DB to reduce footprint. For reranking you can generate smaller vectors for cheap recall and then rely on LLM rerank to sort top candidates.
[02:02] Priya Singh: We're also interested in hybrid search - BM25 + vector. Does Redwood recommend doing hybrid in the vector DB or on application side?
[02:10] Riley Patel: Both are viable. Some vector DBs support hybrid queries natively (Elastic/OpenSearch with dense vectors, or Pinecone + keyword filters). Pattern: use BM25 to filter to a small candidate set, then apply vector similarity, then pass top_k to reranker. That reduces cost and helps precision for things with strong lexical signals like medication names.
[02:27] Ben Carter: For reranking - are customers usually running the reranker inside Redwood hosted inference or on their own infra?
[02:33] Jamie Chen: We see both. Hosted rerank (send candidate list + context to a Redwood generation model) is easiest to start and supports function calling and structured outputs. For customers with PHI, many run rerank in Dedicated or Private so vectors and rerank calls never leave their VPC.
[02:47] Marta Ruiz: Latency targets - we need sub-400ms 95th for search results in the clinician UI. Is that realistic with vector + rerank?
[02:56] Riley Patel: It depends on architecture. Typical split: retrieval (vector DB) 50-150ms, rerank LLM 150-300ms depending on model size and batching. If you rerank top 100 with a medium LLM you'll probably land around 300-500ms. We can optimize by reducing candidate size (top 10-20 with a better recall strategy), using smaller rerank models, or using Dedicated GPUs for lower model latency.
[03:20] Priya Singh: Any advice on candidate generation size vs accuracy for clinical queries?
[03:25] Riley Patel: For clinical content, because of precision needs, we typically do top_k 100 from vector DB then rerank, or hybrid BM25 pre-filter to reduce noise and pull top_k 50. Try a couple of evals: recall@K and rerank MRR.
[03:38] Ben Carter: Storage cost is a concern. Do you support compressed/quantized vectors when shipping to DB?
[03:43] Riley Patel: Compression is DB-side - many support PQ/OPQ, IVF+PQ. Alternatively, you can store float16 or quantized representations. If you want to offload storage, Redwood Dedicated can also host a managed store, but most customers prefer their DB for long-term storage and we provide connectors.
[03:58] Marta Ruiz: On security, what's included for hosted vs dedicated vs private?
[04:03] Jamie Chen: Hosted: standard SOC2, encryption in transit + at rest on our managed service, KMS for key management. Dedicated: isolated GPU pools and network isolation with tenant-level controls. Private: full customer-managed control plane, VPC peering or on-prem option, HSM/KMS integrations, audit logs forwarded to your SIEM. We'll send the security whitepaper and SOC2 report.
[04:24] Priya Singh: We need proof of KMS integration for rotation and HSM.
[04:27] Riley Patel: We'll attach the KMS/hsm integration docs. For private deployments we can integrate with customer KMS via standard APIs.
[04:34] Ben Carter: What about indexing types - approximate NN options affect recall. Any recommendations for acute medication lookups?
[04:42] Riley Patel: For high recall, IVF100+PQ or HNSW with large efSearch works well. For low-latency tight budget, HNSW tuned with smaller efConstruction but higher efSearch can be a sweet spot. Benchmark with your data: we'll help run a small eval.
[04:58] Marta Ruiz: How do we validate model regressions after rolling new embeddings or rerank models?
[05:03] Riley Patel: Redwood Optimize includes evals and quality monitoring - you can run prompt sets and rerank-specific evals to detect regressions. We also recommend canary rollouts and running A/B on a slice of traffic.
[05:15] Ben Carter: For candidate rerank cost - how to estimate?
[05:18] Riley Patel: A rough formula: cost = queries_per_sec * average top_k_rerank * cost_per_rerank_call. We can show sample numbers. For example, 200 QPS * top_k 50 * small rerank model runs on Dedicated GPUs will have predictable throughput and unit cost is lower than hosted pay-as-you-go.
[05:36] Priya Singh: Do you support streaming rerank or do we need to wait for full LLM output?
[05:40] Jamie Chen: You can stream generation responses, but reranking typically needs the model to score each candidate - we usually return a scored list. If you want streaming incremental UI, we can architect partial responses.
[05:51] Marta Ruiz: Any red flags for us? We're worried about vendor lock-in if we use Redwood-specific embeddings.
[05:57] Riley Patel: We steer customers towards open model embeddings or standard vector formats so vectors are portable. You can store vectors in your DB and switch model providers; we provide model versioning and migration guidance.
[06:07] Ben Carter: For the benchmark/POC - what's the recommended plan?
[06:11] Riley Patel: Typical POC: 1) share sample dataset (Priya will share), 2) Redwood runs embedding generation on a subset or you run locally and push vectors, 3) run retrieval + rerank evals using your relevance labels or human evals, 4) measure latency/cost and iterate. We'll help with scripts and an eval notebook.
[06:30] Marta Ruiz: Ok sounds good. Can you also share an architecture diagram for hybrid search + rerank?
[06:35] Jamie Chen: Yes - we'll attach a deck.
[06:38] Ben Carter: Anything else - SSO/SCIM? We use Okta.
[06:41] Riley Patel: We support SAML/Okta for access and RBAC. For Dedicated/Private we can sync groups with SCIM.
[06:49] Priya Singh: One more question - how do you handle embedding drift detection?
[06:53] Riley Patel: Redwood Optimize has quality monitoring and can alert on distributional shifts and drift. We can set thresholds on embedding distance changes or drop in retrieval recall.
[07:03] Jamie Chen: Quick recap and next steps?
[07:05] Marta Ruiz: Yes please.
[07:06] Jamie Chen: Action items: Jamie will send pricing/TCO; Riley will send security docs + KMS notes; Priya will share sample dataset details. We'll schedule a technical deep dive next week to plan the backfill benchmark.
[07:18] Ben Carter: Thanks - that works.
[07:20] Marta Ruiz: Thanks everyone.
